blocks.text: Verses 10–17 present Manasseh’s reversal as a defining movement in the account: after ignoring warning, he is brought into distress, humbles himself, prays, returns to Jerusalem, recognizes the LORD, and removes the foreign worship he had established. This sequence belongs to a recurring pattern in Judah’s royal narratives in which seeking the LORD, humility, prayer, and turning away from prior wrongdoing are set alongside the response to prophetic instruction.
